documents.title: Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors - Transcript
Presentation - Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors on October 29, 2026
Recording - Conference Call with the Fund Managers, Analysts and Investors on October 29, 2026

analysis.summary: Wheels India reported its Q2 and H1 FY27 financial performance, showing growth in sales and export revenues. Management outlined its capex estimates for FY27 along with expansion plans across various product divisions such as auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, and energy products. The company also highlighted strategies focused on export growth, working capital optimization, cost control, and improving return ratios like ROCE and RONW. Wheels India Limited reported its Q1 FY27 financial results, showing a consolidated gross revenue of 1,492.79 Cr and PAT of 38.94 Cr. Management outlined strategic focus areas including growing exports of construction and agricultural tractor wheels, ramping up the expanded machining facility for large windmill castings, and growing the hydraulic cylinder and bus air suspension businesses.

guidance.claim: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs.
guidance.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

capex_expansion.claim: The capex is towards expansion of capacity in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels and air suspension.
capex_expansion.quote: This capex is towards expansion of capacity in auto steel wheels, cast alloy wheels, energy products division including large machining, hydraulic cylinders, construction & mining wheels and air suspension .

capex_expansion.claim: The company spent INR261 crores towards capex in the previous year across windmills, aluminium, and off-road businesses.
capex_expansion.quote: In terms of capex, last year, we basically spent about INR261 crores towards capex, which is both in terms of investment towards the windmill business, aluminium business and a little bit of the off-road businesses and some routine capex and cost savings totalling INR261 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Management expects capex in the current year to be between INR280 crores and INR300 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: And we expect in the current year, it will be between INR280 crores to INR300 crores of capex.

capex_expansion.claim: Aluminium wheel capacity is being increased to 60,000 wheels per month in a few months, and then to 80,000 wheels by half year.
capex_expansion.quote: We are increasing it -- in a few months we are increasing it to 60,000 and then by half year, we'll increase it to 80,000.

margins_costs.claim: Cost optimization, with a thrust on profitability is listed as part of key strategies and focus areas going forward.
margins_costs.quote: Cost optimization, with a thrust on profitability

margins_costs.claim: The net forex profit was about INR4 crores for the quarter and close to INR10 crores for the whole year.
margins_costs.quote: So in the current quarter, we had a profit of about INR4 crores as a net thing on the forex. And for the whole year, it is about close to INR10 crores as forex gain.

margins_costs.claim: Inventory provisions were higher due to the adoption of a more stringent phased provisioning rule.
margins_costs.quote: And inventory provisions are higher because a company has adopted a more stringent rule for provisioning. As a consequence, the provision for inventory has been higher in this quarter as well as for the whole year.

orders_capacity.claim: Combined passenger car steel wheels capacity between Wheels India and its subsidiary is about 11 million to 12 million.
orders_capacity.quote: So if you take passenger car, steel wheels between us and our subsidiary, if I look at it combined, I think Wheels India has got a capacity of about 4 million and the subsidiary has got a capacity of about 7 million. So about 11 million to 12 million is the capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: The tractor wheel capacity for larger wheels stands at 50,000 a month.
orders_capacity.quote: take the tractor industry, if you count it in terms of the larger wheels as opposed to the smaller wheels, we have a capacity of 50,000 a month.

orders_capacity.claim: Commercial vehicle capacity including LCV is about 250,000.
orders_capacity.quote: Commercial vehicle space, if you look at it, we have a capacity -- including the light commercial vehicle, if you look at it, we have about 250,000 capacity and we'll probably look at increasing that to 300,000 capacity.

orders_capacity.claim: Aluminium wheels capacity is currently about 42,000 per month.
orders_capacity.quote: In aluminium wheels we currently have a capacity of about 42,000 per month.

capital_allocation.claim: Management plans to fund capex predominantly through accruals and holding the debt at current levels.
capital_allocation.quote: Fund capex predominantly thro accruals and holding the debt at current levels

capital_allocation.claim: Debt has been stable to declining, and debt equity and debt-to-EBITDA have improved.
capital_allocation.quote: Our debt has been stable to declining. Debt equity has improved. Debt-to-EBITDA has improved and free cash flows are reasonably strong, especially when you compare it to the COVID period and immediate past.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company noted that CBAM tax liability was introduced in Europe from 1st January, resulting in provisions booked under other expenses.
risks_headwinds.quote: from 1st January, CBAM was introduced in Europe. So one of our products which we export to Europe has a CBAM tax liability, which is provided and it is booked under other expenses.

management_commitments.claim: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs.
management_commitments.quote: Capex of FY27 is estimated to be in the region of Rs 400 to Rs 450 crs

management_commitments.claim: Management expects to reach double-digit EBITDA within 1 or 2 years.
management_commitments.quote: So I think as and when that happens, I think we're probably 2 years away -- 1 or 2 years away from double-digit EBITDA. I don't think it should take longer than that.

management_commitments.claim: Management expects ROCE to be 18% plus and return on equity to be 15% plus.
management_commitments.quote: I would look at our ROCE being 18% plus, I would look at our return on equity to be 15% plus.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
